x: On the ninth relay yet another of our Internationals, that great character Bert Footer, showed his teeth and took us into third place, which was well held to the end by our Captain, Bill Webb.

Then came the Bels- Pyer, Penny, Duffett, Bill Webb and so on, and we won with 77pts, to the 275 of Ashcombe and 276 of TVH. A fortnight later the event moved to Wimbledon where there were over 100 starters, 60 of them Belgravians.

In 1929 Harry Hare, the first Belgrave President ever of the S.T.C.C.A., handed to his club mates the DEWAR Shield for winning the Championship (for the first time), and the six team winners medals to:- BILL MITCHELL (4), ARTHUR PENNY (7), ARTHUR ALLUM (12), BILL WEBB (16), PAUL KHLOPIN (23) and ALEC ROBERTSHAW (26).
Frank and Bill Webb for their comradeship on those wonderful all day strolls over Ranmore and Leith Hill, with Frank no matter what the weather, emerging debonair as ever.

We are pleased to see Bill Webb fully recovered from his serious illness. Turning to the competitive fields, we did not lay claim to any major team titles, but there were many fine individual performances by Club members spread throughout the various sections and age groups.

He was pleasantly surprised when he attended the celebrations for Bill Webb's 90th Birthday for at the end of the proceedings Clive Shippen presented Arthur with an inscribed silver salver commemorating his fine win of fifty years ago.

Micky was Club mile champion in both 1922 and 1923 and was our 3rd scorer in the 1928 "National" behind Bill Webb and Bert Footer. His name also appeared on the Belgrave 7 miles and 10 miles cross-country trophies.

I found the item about "Bill" Webb very interesting. He was once described to me as "a real gentleman." I would think that he would have had an opinion on the article but would have been far too modest to own up to the description of him so well drawn by Clive.
Like Bill Webb before him he maintained a fervent interest in the Club, as his family were only too aware. On his 90th birthday his niece made him a wonderful birthday cake.

Some things never change and it was announced that we had new Club vests and it is nice to read names which echo down the years - Tommy Green, Bill Webb, Ernie Duffett and Bert Footer, all still actively involved more than 40 years later.
Bill Webb ran the race of his life and played a true Captain’s role as he held on to third place – and up front Salford again wrested the lead from Birchfield Harriers.
